items.name: Godrick's Great Rune
items.japanese_name: ゴドリックの大ルーン (Godorikku no Dai Rūn)
items.effect: Boosts all stats by +5.
items.summary:
Godrick's Great Rune is a Great Rune in Elden Ring.

Great Runes are Key Items obtained upon defeating Shardbearers. They can be equipped while resting at a Site of Grace and once activated by using a Rune Arc, grant the Tarnished passive abilities, lasting until death.
items.description:
The Great Rune of the shardbearer Godrick, devoid of any benediction.
Seek the Divine Tower of Limgrave, which stands beyond the great bridge from Stormveil Castle.
effect_details: After equipping the Great Rune at any Site of Grace, upon consuming a Rune Arc all attributes will be raised by 5 levels.

details: Upon defeat of Godrick the Grafted.
Restored at the Divine Tower of Limgrave, accessible from the sending gate past the Limgrave Tower Bridge Site of Grace within Stormveil Castle.

notes: Great Runes will be lost upon entering New Game Plus and, once re-obtained, they'll have to be restored again.
The stat boosting effect of this Great Rune also provides an increase to defense, as regular leveling does.

Compared Radahn's Great Rune, the latter only outperforms the former at 37 Vigor and 40 Mind, although it always provides a better boost to Endurance; meanwhile Morgott's Great Rune offers a better HP boost from 16 Vigor onwards.

effect_details: Equipping and activating the great rune with a Rune Arc grants the following effects:

→ The Blessing of Blood has infinite duration.
→ When blessed spirits kill an enemy, the user of the Great Rune will be healed by 10% of their maximum HP, similar to the Taker's Cameo talisman.

When invading another world while the Great Rune is active:

As the invader arrives to the invaded world, they receives 3 copies of a temporary unique consumable item, called Phantom Great Rune. When consumed, a small red area-of-effect is created which grants enemies in close proximity the Blessing of Blood. When invading, this is the only way to apply the Blessing of Blood.

details: Obtained upon defeat of Mohg, Lord of Blood in Mohgwyn Palace.
Restored at the Divine Tower of East Altus found past the elevator used to access the Forbidden Lands.

notes: The Blessing of Blood's damage buff on summoned spirits stacks with the Lord of Blood's Exultation (should the Spirit be the Mimic Tear Ashes with that talisman equipped).

A crystal tear formed slowly over the ages, where the scattered sap of the Scadutree pools deep within the furnace golems.

Can be mixed in the Flask of Wondrous Physick. The resulting concoction temporarily enhances spontaneous guard.

effect_details: For 300 seconds: guarding will increase physical guard negation by 100% and non-physical guard negations by 75%, and decrease incoming stamina damage by 65% for 6 frames/0.20 seconds; spamming block will reduce deflect frames/seconds to 3/0.10, 2/0.07, then 0.

If an attack is blocked within those 6 frames: guard counters will receive a buff that has multiple tiers. Subsequent deflects while the buff is still active will increase the current tier and reset the duration to 5 seconds, and some attacks being deflected can gain multiple tiers at a time.
- Tier 1: increases damage by 20% (15% against other players), stamina damage by 20%, and poise and stance damage by 15% for 5 seconds.
- Tier 2: increases damage by 40% (28% against other players), stamina damage by 40%, and poise and stance damage by 23% for 5 seconds.
- Tier 3: increases damage by 60% (36% against other players), stamina damage by 60%, and poise and stance damage by 31% for 5 seconds.
- Tier 4: increases damage by 80% (45% against other players), stamina damage by 80%, and poise and stance damage by 39% for 5 seconds.

effect_details: For 180 seconds after using the Flask of Wondrous Physick, activate the following effect:

Grants a damage bonus upon attaining a certain amount of "points" from landing melee weapon attacks and certain spells: gaining 17/30/45/60 points increases Attack Power by 9%/13%/20%/20%. 1 point is lost every 0.5/1/0.7/0.4 seconds that has passed since a point has been gained.

notes: Point gain from melee weapon attacks is largely independent of weapon class: most weapons gain 8 points per light attack of any kind (including dual wield attacks), 10 points per heavy attack or jumping heavy attack, and 14 points per charged heavy attack or guard counter.
→ Daggers, Throwing Blades, Backhand Blades, Fists, Hand-to-Hand, Claws, Beast Claws, Perfume Bottles, Sacred Seals, Torches, and Small Shields only gain 6 points per light attack hit.
→ Multi-hit attacks gain points every time they hit: as an example, the two-handed light attacks of Claws hit twice and such give 6+6=12 points if both hits land.

→ Some exceptions: Fire Knight's Greatsword and Godslayer's Greatsword gain 14 points per light attack, the Ruins Greatsword gain 20 points per charged heavy attack, Claws of Night and Smithscript Cirque gain 0 points per heavy attack of any kind, any Fists weapon gain 8 points per two-handed light attack (16 points in total, since it hits twice) if the deal Strike damage, and Great Spears gain only 6 points for each of the first two hits of running heavy attacks and 10 for the final hit.

→ Adula's Moonblade (melee hit only) and Carian Greatsword gain 10 points, Gavel of Haima gains 20 points, Carian Piercer gains 14 points, Carian Slicer gains 4 points, and Rock Blaster gains 2 points.

Golden prosthesis once used by the one-armed valkyrie. A masterwork of craftsmanship, with practice and skill it can be used as proficiently as a real arm.

A keepsake of the warrior jar Alexander. Found at the core of the dead flesh that once filled the great jar.

items.description:
Pure white oath-cloth given by Varré. The final trial to be anointed a Knight of Mohg, Lord of Blood.

"Soak the cloth with a maiden's blood... The blood of anyone's maiden will do. You are maidenless, after all."

On the Night of the Black Knives, someone stole a fragment of Death from Maliketh, the Black Blade, and imbued its power into the assassins' daggers.

Cursemark of Death is a Key Item in Elden Ring.

Cursemark carved into the discarded flesh of Ranni the Witch.Also known as the half-wheel wound of the centipede.

This cursemark was carved at the moment of Death of the first demigod, and should have taken the shape of a circle.

However, two demigods perished at the same time, breaking the cursemark into two half-wheels.

Ranni was the first of the demigods whose flesh perished, while the Prince of Death perished in soul alone.

Seedbed Curse is a Key Item in Elden Ring.

Curse grown on a corpse killed and defiled by the Dung Eater. A tender pox afflicted with omen horns.

The Dung Eater cultivates the seedbed curse on corpses.

By doing so he prevents dead souls returning to the Erdtree, leaving them forever cursed. One of the most loathsome things found in all the Lands Between.

Sellen's Primal Glintstone is a Key Item in Elden Ring.

items.description:
Glintstone from within the sorceress Sellen's body. Seemingly half-alive, blood vessels are visible within.

"My apprentice, do you think it distasteful?"

Be summoned to challenge Sorceress Sellen?: invade Sellen and help Witch-Hunter Jerren kill her to be awarded with the Witch's Glintstone Crown and Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone x1.
Be summoned to assist Sorceress Sellen?: join Sellen as a cooperator and help her kill Jerren to be awarded with his Eccentric's Set.

Seluvis's Potion is a Key Item in Elden Ring.

items.description:
Small flask received from Preceptor Seluvis containing a cloudy tonic of bluish black.

"Find Nepheli, and ensure she drinks it."

Gideon Ofnir: select Give Gideon Seluvis's Potion to have him dispose of it.

Scroll bearing a royal coat of arms. A letter of introduction written by Preceptor Seluvis.

An ephemeral sliver that gives off a pale amber glow. What remains of a passing flash of starlight.

If the stars command our fates, then amber-hued stars must command the fates of the gods. Such is the belief that inspired the use of these shards to prepare a most special draught.

Amber Draught is a Key Item in Elden Ring.

Small flask received from Preceptor Seluvis containing a gleaming amber draught for use in a scheme.

The hidden treasure of the Eternal City of Nokron; a blade said to have been born of a corpse.

This blood-drenched fetish is proof of the high treason committed by the Eternal City and symbolizes its downfall.

Cannot be wielded by those without a fate, but is said to be able to harm the Greater Will and its vassals.

infobox.item_effect: Give to Ranni to receive the Carian Inverted Statue.

items.japanese_name: 小さなラニ (Chiisana Rani)

items.description:
A doll resembling Ranni the Witch. From head to toe every detail is perfect.

This unresponsive doll seems pleasantly cool.

text: [Description]
[Acquisition and use]
Found in a coffin on the northernmost, upper level of the Ainsel River once Ranni has been given the Fingerslayer Blade.

[Description]
[Acquisition and use]
Replaces the lively miniature after defeating the Baleful Shadow by the sluice gate just before the Lake of Rot in Ainsel River.
Serves no practical use and is only a mere souvenir of your short journey together.

Dark Moon Ring is a Key Item in Elden Ring.

Ring depicting a leaden full moon. Symbolic of a cold oath, the ring is supposed to be given by Lunar Princess Ranni to her consort.

Ranni is an Empyrean, meaning her consort would by rights earn the title of lord.

A warning is engraved within; "Whoever thou mayest be, take not the ring from this place, the solitude beyond the night is better mine alone."

A source that gives rise to Those Who Live in Death.

Once upon a time, the stars of the night sky guided fate, and this is a recollection of those times.
